Where to Stay in Chachoengsao?

heroSub: 12 hand-picked Chachoengsao hotels across every budget — town-centre hotels near Wat Sothon, boutiques on the Bang Pakong River, a stay beside the 100-year-old Ban Mai market, plus stays near the industrial estate and budget guesthouses. Covering the town centre, Bang Pakong, Bang Khla and Khlong Khuean. From roughly ฿550–1,500/night.
introH2: 🛕 Why does choosing the right area in Chachoengsao matter?
introHtml: Chachoengsao (Paet Riu) is a town close to Bangkok that many people visit on a day trip to pay respects at Wat Sothon and explore the Bang Pakong riverfront — but staying overnight lets you soak up the riverside-town feel far more. Stays are spread across several areas with different vibes — the town centre (Mueang Chachoengsao) is near Wat Sothon, the markets, the railway station and the 100-year-old Ban Mai market, ideal for temple visits and market strolls; the Bang Pakong riverfront has resorts and small river-view stays for a quiet break; Bang Khla district has a floating market and a flying-fox viewing spot; and Bang Pakong district is near the industrial estate and the river mouth, handy for workers or a stopover. Many people book without checking the area and end up driving back and forth to Wat Sothon several times. This guide rounds up 12 hand-picked Chachoengsao hotels across every tier — all with real guest reviews, prices compared across 3 sites and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Chachoengsao has no metro, but it's very close to Bangkok — about a 1–1.5 hour drive — and the eastern-line railway station sits in the town centre, so you can easily arrive by train from Hua Lamphong/Makkasan and visit Wat Sothon without driving. Pick by your itinerary: the town centre (Na Mueang–Bang Tin Pet) is near Wat Sothon, the station, the markets and the 100-year-old Ban Mai market, best if you don't have a car; the Bang Pakong riverfront (Khlong Na–Bang Kaeo–Khlong Khuean) has resorts and river-view stays for a relaxed break; and Bang Pakong–Tha Kham sits near the river mouth, mangroves and the Wellgrow estate, handy for a stopover or workers. Almost every stay has free parking, so they suit self-drivers well.

entries.storyHtml: Heaven Hotel is the town-centre hotel that best balances a high score with a healthy review count — 9.2 from 129 reviews. Opened in 2020, the rooms are still fresh and clean, sitting on Chachoengsao-Bang Pakong Road in town, a few minutes' drive to Wat Sothon and walkable to markets and restaurants. Room types run from Superior up to Suite and Family Room, suiting couples, families and anyone staying overnight for a temple visit — the most well-rounded in-town pick in Paet Riu.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Visit Wat Sothon early before the crowds — it's only a few minutes' drive from here. If your budget stretches, pick a Deluxe, which is roomier and newer than the Superior.

entries.storyHtml: Suanmaithara Resort is a quiet garden resort about 8 minutes' drive from Wat Sothon, scoring 8.8 from 64 reviews. It's a cluster of around 20 rooms set among gardens with parking right outside each room and a leafy feel cut off from road noise. Room types run from Standard up to VIP and a family room, with rates from just ฿800 — ideal for self-drivers who want peace and quiet while still being able to drive into town and reach Wat Sothon easily.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Couples wanting a more spacious room should pick the VIP Room, the largest here; families should go for the family room with an extra bed.

entries.name: Dheva Resort

entries.storyHtml: Dheva Resort is a riverside boutique resort on the Bang Pakong River in a country-farmhouse style, scoring 9.0 from 38 reviews. It's a small resort of around 16 rooms in Khlong Khuean district, quiet and restful, with balconies overlooking the river and the rice fields — ideal for couples or anyone escaping the bustle for a riverside break. There are room-only rates from ฿1,500 plus packages with three meals, perfect if you want a stay where everything is taken care of without going out.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: It's a small resort with few rooms, so it fills fast on weekends — book ahead. For the full experience, pick a meal-inclusive package so you don't have to drive out for food.

entries.storyHtml: The Wish Hotel is the newly opened hotel with the most reviews in this guide — 146, scoring 8.1. It's a 64-room hotel in Bang Phra subdistrict, and its standout point is that every room has a private balcony; the rooms are still new and clean, with rates from just ฿850. It sits on the Bang Phra side of Mueang Chachoengsao, within driving distance of town and Wat Sothon — ideal for self-drivers who want a new, heavily reviewed hotel at a friendly price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Every room has a balcony — ask for a higher floor for an open view and more quiet. If your budget stretches, the King Room is notably roomier than the Deluxe.

It suits anyone wanting resort facilities — pool, spa and river views — in a spot that's still a short drive from town and Wat Sothon.

entries.storyHtml: The Brown House is a boutique hotel with a cafe in an English-cottage style, sitting right by the 100-year-old Ban Mai market, scoring 8.6 from 9 reviews. It's a small stay of around 12 rooms on the Bang Pakong River, some Riverview rooms facing the water, and its draw is that you step out straight into Ban Mai — Paet Riu's famous old riverside market. Ideal for anyone who wants a design-led stay and an old market on the doorstep.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The 100-year Ban Mai market is liveliest at weekends. For the riverside feel, pick a Riverview Room overlooking the Bang Pakong.

Ideal for anyone wanting a natural mangrove riverside setting near the river mouth, in a spot that's an easy drive from Bangkok.

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate and may change by date and season — always check live rates and compare 3 sites before booking. During festivals and long weekends, especially the Luang Pho Sothon worship festival, in-town hotels fill fast, so book 2–4 weeks ahead. Small riverside resorts like Dheva and River Breeze also fill quickly on holidays. Chachoengsao has no metro but is close to Bangkok, about a 1–1.5 hour drive, with an eastern-line railway station in the town centre. Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Chachoengsao hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Chachoengsao?
faq.a: It depends on your plans · the town centre (Mueang Chachoengsao) is near Wat Sothon, the station, the markets and the 100-year-old Ban Mai market, best for temple visits and those without a car (Heaven, JK Living, Kesorn, BB House, The Brown House) · the Bang Pakong riverfront is best for a quiet break (Dheva, Suntara, River Breeze) · Bang Pakong is near the estate and the river mouth, good for workers or a stopover (Wellgrow, Ratathara)

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chachoengsao hotels cost?
faq.a: Chachoengsao is friendly on the wallet: budget 2-star stays start around ฿550–700 (Kesorn, BB House, Wellgrow) · in-town 3-star hotels around ฿790–850 (Heaven, JK Living, Suanmaithara, The Wish) · riverside resorts and boutiques (3–4 star) from around ฿1,000–1,500 (Ratathara, Dheva, Suntara, The Brown House)

faq.q: ❓ Visiting Wat Sothon — which hotel is conveniently close?
faq.a: In-town stays a few minutes' drive from Wat Sothon and walkable to markets are Heaven Hotel (฿790, scores 9.2), BB House (฿650) and Kesorn Boutique (฿550, cheapest) · while Suanmaithara Resort (฿800) is a quiet garden resort about 8 minutes' drive from Wat Sothon

faq.q: ❓ Which Chachoengsao hotel has a swimming pool?
faq.a: In this guide the one with a pool is Suntara Wellness Resort & Hotel, a riverside wellness resort on the Bang Pakong with both a pool and a spa, from ฿1,400 — ideal for a proper resort-style getaway

faq.q: ❓ Want to stay on the Bang Pakong River — which to pick?
faq.a: For a quiet riverside stay · Dheva Resort ฿1,500 riverside boutique with rice-field views in Khlong Khuean, scores 9.0 · River Breeze ฿900 small riverside stay in Bang Kaeo · Ratathara Resort ฿1,000 mangrove riverside houses by the river mouth in Bang Pakong · all are easiest with a car

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Chachoengsao hotel?
faq.a: On ordinary weekdays 1–2 weeks ahead is enough, as Chachoengsao is close to Bangkok and not crowded · but during the Luang Pho Sothon worship festival and long weekends, in-town hotels and small riverside resorts like Dheva fill very fast, so book 2–4 weeks or more ahead
